vid_urls.title: U.S. Spacewalk 100
vid_urls.description:
Join us for a spacewalk milestone!

NASA astronaut Anil Menon and CSA (Canadian Space Agency) astronaut Joshua Kutryk are participating in the 100th spacewalk conducted from the International Space Station's Quest airlock without the space shuttle present. This will be the 285th spacewalk conducted to build, maintain, and upgrade the orbiting laboratory.

Menon and Kutryk are expected to begin their spacewalk at about 8:10 a.m. EDT (1210 UTC); they'll be installing a new International Space Station Roll-Out Solar Array (IROSA), which will boost the station's power.

Learn more about today's spacewalk: https://go.nasa.gov/4yRBm97
Get daily updates from the space station: https://www.nasa.gov/blogs/spacestation/

image.name: US EVA Astronaut outside the ISS

results.description: NASA astronaut Anil Menon and CSA astronaut Joshua Kutryk will exit the station’s Quest airlock to install and deploy an International Space Station Roll-Out Solar Array (IROSA) on the 2A electrical power channel. The solar array will be the seventh IROSA and will provide additional power to support critical station operations, including its safe and controlled deorbit.

image.name: US EVA Astronaut outside the ISS

results.description:
NASA astronaut Anil Menon and CSA astronaut Joshua Kutryk will install and deploy the eighth and final IROSA on the 3B channel of the space station, completing the power augmentation upgrades.

The final two roll-out solar arrays will complete the space station’s power system augmentation. Together, the eight roll-out arrays will increase available power by up to 30%, boosting the station’s electric power generation capacity from 160 kilowatts to approximately 215 kilowatts.

info_urls.title: Solar Orbiter: journey around the Sun
info_urls.description: Solar Orbiter: journey around the Sun

results.description: Solar Orbiter, a partnership between ESA and NASA, will perform a gravity assist maneuver with Venus on December 24, 2026. Throughout its mission it also makes repeated gravity assist flybys of Venus to get closer to the Sun, and to change its orbital inclination, boosting it out of the ecliptic plane, to get the best – and first – views of the Sun’s poles.
